headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Plane can ingest files and egress broadly while the prompt-engineering repo is an unverified content source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing repository with no runtime protections or I/O surfaces documented, while B can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks. If A’s content is copied into B, B may treat attacker-controlled text as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible but not proven by direct interaction evidence, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted or uploaded into agent_b
IF agent_b parses uploaded text as instructions or task content
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to plain-text previews for imported content
Add a manual review step before any pasted prompt content is acted on
Tag imported files from agent_a as untrusted in agent_b
Use separate workspaces for prompt libraries and task execution
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has broad network egress and file-upload surfaces, while A is a docs-only content repository with no sensitive data classes listed. If A’s files or notes are moved into B, B can transmit them externally. The pairwise leakage path exists in default B configurations, but the blast radius is limited by A’s documented data profile, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a content is uploaded into agent_b
IF agent_b sends uploaded file contents to external APIs or services
mitigations: Avoid uploading agent_a artifacts into agent_b
Disable external integrations on agent_b for imported files
Review outbound destinations in agent_b before use
Store prompt-library content in a separate repository
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists for agent_b

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write or network capabilities, while B cannot write the filesystem but can run multiple instances and has broad egress. There is no shared mutable write surface in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains about hidden orchestrator state, so low rather than none.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF shared state is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant shared write access to the same directory
Run only one writer for any shared resource
Check orchestrator locking before parallel runs
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt-engineering content source, and B handles issues, tasks, and roadmaps. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative guidance, errors or misleading instructions can cascade into task creation or scheduling decisions. Because B has downstream action surfaces and no verification mechanism is documented, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF agent_b creates or updates tasks based on unverified content from agent_a
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs before task creation
Mark imported guidance as advisory only in agent_b
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Limit agent_b automation to draft mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A is an open-source content repo with no touched data classes, while B exposes file uploads and external contact channels. The compliance pathway is therefore speculative and limited to configuration choices, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into agent_b
IF deployment settings impose residency or retention constraints not met by agent_b
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in agent_b uploads
Review retention settings before use
Document the deployment region for agent_b
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows from general task tracking
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
